source.rationale: The zero-hit close. An empty (but successful) probe is a MEASURED zero, not a failure, so the node is entitled to say so - and it says it once, in a sentence, instead of leaving the customer to read three '- no delivery' suffixes and infer it. Distinguishing this from hand-annotate-probe-failed-renders-bare is the entire reason D2 exists: same rendered shape upstream, opposite entitlement to make a claim. customer_probe_hits is 0 here and null there. RETUNED 2026-08-25 (90-day probe window): the probe now always sends a delivery-date window - the parser's own bounds, else an injected last-90-days default - so the miss suffix and the zero-hit close stay bounded to that window; a bare '- no delivery' would be a false universal, the probe never looked further back. REPIN captain copy decision 2026-08-25: window wording dropped, 'recent' keeps the claim bounded - the defaulted-arm strings are now '- no recent delivery' and 'None of these have a recent delivery.' (naming 'the last 90 days' read like a search limit; the probe window itself is unchanged at 90 days). The parser ctx entry here carries NEITHER date bound, which is exactly the defaulted-window case; hand-annotate-customer-dated-window.json pins the other arm. customer_probe_window_days is the diagnostic mirror of that rule (90 = defaulted window, null = the customer's own dates).
